Older Americans Month: Champion Your Health
Every May, Older Americans Month recognizes the contributions of older adults, highlights aging trends, and reaffirms commitments to serve our older community members. The 2026 theme is “Champion Your Health”.Throughout the month of May, Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community, Oxford Area are partnering to highlight and offer programming focused on promoting physical, mental, and emotional health and well-being at all ages.You can participate by playing “Community BINGO” with us! It’s as easy as 1, 2, 3!1) Print your own or pick up a Community Bingo card at any of the following locations:Oxford Seniors, 922 Tollgate Dr., OxfordOxford Lane Library, 441 S. Locust St.The Knolls of Oxford, Clubhouse or Front DeskScripps Gerontology Center, 396 Upham Hall, on campus2) Every time you do something listed on the card, mark it off. The goal is to get “BINGO” as many times as possible. A “BINGO” is marking off any 5 squares in a straight line – either vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.3) Bring your completed BINGO card to the Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sun. May 31 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and FUN!

summary: Celebrate **Older Americans Month** in May by playing **Community BINGO**! Pick up a card at Oxford Seniors (922 Tollgate Dr.), Oxford Lane Library (441 S. Locust St.), The Knolls of Oxford, or Scripps Gerontology Center (396 Upham Hall). Complete activities like attending chair yoga, visiting parks, making art, attending concerts, and connecting with neighbors. Bring your completed card to the **Intergenerational BINGO Party on May 31, 3:00-5:00 PM** at Oxford Seniors for prizes and snacks.

Thank you for supporting the Oxford Lions Club! Thanks!

**Action for Healthy Kids** presents **Every Kid Healthy Week from April 20th-24th** with daily themed activities:

- **Tasty Tuesday (April 21)**: Try new foods, help prepare meals, have an indoor picnic

Families are encouraged to take pictures participating in activities and post on social media with **#HealthyLikeRox**.

title: Allergies or Cold: Know the Difference
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Nurse's 

Notes

Nurse's Notes

summary: The school nurse provides a flowchart to help distinguish between allergy symptoms and cold symptoms. **Key differences**: Allergies typically involve clear mucus, seasonal occurrence, itchiness, and symptoms that last for extended periods. Colds usually present with green or yellow mucus, fever, body discomfort, and symptoms that come on quickly and taper off fairly rapidly. **Call your doctor if** symptoms last longer than two weeks, symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

title: PAX Good Behavior Game Program
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
PAX

PAX

The PAX Good Behavior Game is a research-based classroom strategy that helps children make positive choices, and collaborate with others. It supports a calmer, more focused learning environment by promoting kindness, teamwork, and respectful behavior.

summary:
The **PAX Good Behavior Game** is a research-based classroom strategy that helps students make positive choices and collaborate with others. It promotes a calmer, more focused learning environment through kindness, teamwork, and respectful behavior.

The April 2026 student calendar includes daily PAX activities such as National Walking Day (April 3), World Health Day (April 6), Earth Day activities (April 22), and National Superhero Day (April 28), along with prompts for students to practice leadership, gratitude, and positive behaviors throughout the month.
